records.title: The effect of delay on treatment outcome in altitude-induced decompression sickness.
records.locator: Methods, p. 687, and Results and Tables I–II, p. 688
records.evidence_note: This USAFSAM treatment file review excludes flying, diving, cases treated outside USAF hyperbaric chambers, and cases without recompression. Duty position is not reported. The table gives 29 cases at altitude and 99 in the first two hours, totaling 128/233 (54.9%). The narrative says 67%. Three printed bin percentages in Table II differ from their respective counts divided by 233 when rounded to one decimal place.

observations.group: Treated chamber cases in the USAFSAM files
observations.note: No exposure population by duty position or as a whole is given for this series.

observations.group: All 233 treated chamber DCS records, including one unknown onset
observations.note: Derived by adding the two printed count rows. The Results text gives a conflicting 67%. The denominator is the full table total.

records.title: The risk of developing decompression sickness during air travel following altitude chamber flight.
records.locator: Methods and Results, pp. 1028–1029 and Tables I–II
records.evidence_note: The review screened USAFSAM treatment charts from 1966 through 1987. The displayed treated-student series covers 1982–1987. Inside observers and students treated with surface oxygen alone were explicitly excluded. The paper gives approximate annual training volumes by personal communication and no exact denominator linked to the case series or to subsequent air travel.

observations.group: Chamber students in the published series
observations.locator: Methods, Results and Table II, pp. 1028–1029
observations.note: The existing v1.4 timing data are a conditional decomposition of this same 292-case series. The seven after air travel are a nested subset of delayed cases. The paper excludes inside-observer cases.

records.title: Altitude decompression sickness: hyperbaric therapy results in 528 cases.
records.locator: Methods and Results, pp. 833–834, Table I, p. 834, and Tables III–V, p. 835
records.evidence_note: The 1977–1986 case review covers 507 chamber and 21 actual flight cases. Table III gives 402 student and 93 physiological trainer chamber cases. Table IV applies to 1979–1986. Table V places peripheral nervous system symptoms under Type I. Rudge and Shafer use a peripheral nervous system/spinal row under Type II. The labels are preserved as printed.

derived_effects.method: unadjusted log risk ratio Wald interval under independent binomial observations

printed_interval_reproduction_check.note: This numerical check nearly reproduces the published bounds and does not verify the original calculation.

records.evidence_note: The conventional unadjusted analysis returns approximately 0.787–1.276 under either interpretation. It assumes independent exposures, makes no allowance for repeated staff exposures, and cannot establish the variance used by the authors. The published interval and the derived checks are retained with their own provenance.

observations.note: Printed 95% CI 0.0956 to 10.5021. The supplementary record contains separate unadjusted recalculations.
